newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung to invest 7 trln won in non-memory chips.
newsitem.headline: Samsung to invest 7 trln won in non-memory chips.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Group said it would invest seven trillion won in non-memory chip production over the next five years.

A statement, dated Wednesday but sent to Reuters on Thursday, said the aim was to achieve $15 billion turnover in non-memory chips by 2005, accounting for 50 percent of total Samsung semiconductor sales, up from 20 percent now.
By 2005 Samsung hoped to have five percent of the global market in non-memory chips against its current two percent, the statement said.

Samsung would also spend four trillion won by 2005 developing thin-film transistor liquid crystal displays, code division multiple access stations, central processing units, application specific integrated circuits, lithium batteries and in the chemical, environmental and bio-engineering areas.
The group was seeking three trillion won profit on 19 trillion won turnover in 2005 from its four trillion won investment, the statement said.
